title: Align eval metrics and consensus judging for staged config/model rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: We need a repeatable, auditable method to compare pre- and post-change model/config behavior that produces a single actionable signal for rollout gating. This ticket defines a harmonized scoring pipeline (mapping heterogeneous task-specific metrics into a canonical harmonized score), a consensus LLM-judge adjudication protocol with calibration, and a per-config sensitivity analysis ("dose-response" curves) so PMs/Eng can set SLO-aware rollout thresholds. The goal is to reduce false positive regressions and surface real quality regressions tied to model or serving config changes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical harmonized_score is computed for each eval run and documented with transformation rules for at least three task families (QA, summarization, instruction-following)
LLM-judge pool protocol implemented: 3 distinct judge models, vote-weighting by calibrated confidence, and bootstrapped CI estimation for final score
Calibration mapping (judge_confidence -> empirical accuracy) computed and versioned; documented calibration drift check added to nightly pipeline
Dose-response sensitivity dashboards available per config knob (temperature, max_tokens, batching strategy, quantization profile) with recommended safe thresholds
Clear rollout gating rule exists in Console: automatic block or auto-rollback when harmonized_score drop > 2.0 points with 95% CI excluding zero, or per-customer tunable thresholds
technical_notes: Harmonized score will be an affine transform of task-level metrics followed by weighted averaging across intents; weights are configurable per project and default to F1-like metrics for classification and ROUGE/CHRF for text quality tasks

LLM-as-judge pool: start with three model families (redwood/open-adjudicator-1, openai-moderate, open-source-judger-v2); each judge returns label + scalar confidence; we calibrate via isotonic regression per-judge per-task family
Compute bootstrap CIs via 2000 bootstrap samples per run to estimate score uncertainty; use stratified sampling by intent and length buckets
Dose-response experiments: sweep single knob at a time on a representative 5k prompt set; fit a local linear model to detect inflection points and 95% CIs
Latency of adjudication is expected to add ~15-30ms per sample (parallelizable); budget this into CI window for nightly runs
